questions.q: Which of the following will not give \($\mathrm{HVZ}$\) reaction?
questions.solution: In H.V.Z reaction, in presence of small amount of phosphorus, aliphatic carboxylic acids containing \($\alpha$\)-hydrogen atom reacts with \($\mathrm{Cl}}_{2},  \mathrm{Br}$}_{2}\) to yield an acid halide in which \($\alpha$\)-hydrogen has been replaced by halogen. So, trichloroethanoic acid, among the given options which do not contains \($\alpha$\)-hydrogen atom, will not give \($\mathrm{HVZ}$\) reaction.

questions.q: When propionic acid is treated with aqueous \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3, \mathrm{CO}_2\) is liberated. The \(\mathrm{C}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) comes from
questions.solution:
Carboxylic acids decompose bicarbonates into \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) gas and \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) to form sodium salts of carboxylic acids.
So, \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) comes from \(\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}\)of \(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\)
